events.title: Marine life crucial to regulating atmospheric CO₂ levels
events.one_liner: Marine organisms regulate atmospheric CO₂ through the biological carbon pump, sequestering approximately 10 billion tonnes annually—over one quarter of human fossil-fuel emissions. Without marine life, CO₂ levels would rise 50% in pre-industrial scenarios, with mangroves and seagrasses sequestering carbon at rates up to four times higher than terrestrial forests.
takeaways: Marine organisms sequester ~10 billion tonnes CO₂ annually (>¼ of fossil-fuel emissions)
Without marine life, CO₂ would increase 50% (pre-industrial scenario), causing 1.6°C warming
Mangroves store average 1,000 tonnes carbon per hectare; sequester 4× faster than terrestrial forests
Biological carbon pump more important than solubility pump for modern ocean CO₂ sequestration

events.title: Prescribed Fire Reduces Giant Sequoia Mortality by More Than Half During Severe Wildfire
events.one_liner: A study from Mountain Home Demonstration State Forest in California's Sierra Nevada found that prescribed fire treatments cut giant sequoia tree mortality by over 50% during the 2020 Castle Fire. The research demonstrates that strategic prescribed burning—mimicking the fire regime these ancient trees evolved with—can enhance their resilience to increasingly severe wildfires in the context of a warming climate.
takeaways: Prescribed fire reduced giant sequoia mortality by more than half during the 2020 Castle Fire at Mountain Home Demonstration State Forest
Study conducted in the world's largest giant sequoia grove in the southern Sierra Nevada
Research from University of Nevada, Reno College of Agriculture, Biotechnology & Natural Resources
Giant sequoias evolved with fire over millennia but face unprecedented mortality from severe wildfires after ~200 years of fire suppression

events.title: Physical Activity Far Outweighs Diet for Longevity, New Review Finds
events.one_liner: A narrative review published in Mayo Clinic Proceedings finds that physical activity and cardiorespiratory fitness have a dramatically stronger association with longevity than diet quality. Sedentary behavior increases mortality risk by 46–163%, while poor diet raises it only 3–20%; conversely, adding 2,000 daily steps reduces mortality risk by 25–50%, compared to 13% from doubling fruit intake.
takeaways: Physical inactivity increases all-cause mortality risk by 46–163%, versus 3–20% for poor diet
Achieving 11,000–16,000 daily steps associates with 45–67% lower mortality risk vs. 2,000–5,000 steps
Adding just 2,000 steps daily reduces mortality risk by 25–50% in sedentary people
Among highly sedentary individuals, 5–10 more minutes of daily activity corresponds to 30–42% lower death risk
